title: Principle 7: Retention: Don't fill a leaky bucket
coreMove: Protect important gains with planned returns before fluent work quietly leaks away.
sourcePressure: Retention addresses fast forgetting and the need to revisit important material after one successful encounter. The source sidecar contains no named people, studies, institutions, places, dates, or artifacts for this chapter, so named source anchors must be omitted rather than invented.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Trying to preserve everything forever or assuming one good session locks a skill in place.

hook: Ch10: learner stares at browser tabs and realizes motivation is not enough
Ch10: broad modern world pressure opener
counterintuition: The obvious move is not the real move
Most people think more effort is enough
This is not about working harder
tryThisNow: Spend one minute thinking about your learning journey

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Olivia, a clinic receptionist revisiting a referral workflow before the monthly rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia rehearses the referral workflow before the monthly clinic rush and notices the step that has already gone soft.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a referral stamp beside a half-filled clinic form

exampleSpecs.domain: Jack, a physics student rebuilding yesterday's method at the board
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jack rebuilds yesterday's physics method at the board without notes and writes the missing step into a revisit slot.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dusty eraser ledge under an unfinished force diagram

exampleSpecs.domain: Olivier, a language learner choosing which phrases deserve scheduled returns
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier chooses ten field phrases that must survive next month and leaves the decorative vocabulary alone.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pocket phrase card clipped to a train ticket

exampleSpecs.domain: Min, a firefighter refreshing a rarely used equipment sequence
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress

exampleSpecs.domain: Frida, a procurement analyst repairing a plan that treated one clean run as permanent

skillTargets: schedule returns before important gains leak

tryThisNowSpec: List three gains you cannot afford to lose and schedule the next return for only the most important one.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
